content: Illicium, commonly referred to as the anise tree or anise-tree, is a genus of flowering plants that comprises 42 species of evergreen shrubs and small trees. It is the only genus within the family Illiciaceae. These species are native to tropical and subtropical regions, including eastern and southeastern Asia, southeastern North America, and the West Indies. Illicium anisatum (Japanese Star Anise) is found in southern Japan and Taiwan. Illicium arborescens is native to Taiwan. Illicium floridanum (Purple Anise or Florida Anise) is indigenous to the southeastern United States. Illicium henryi (Henry's Anise) is native to southwestern China. Illicium lanceolatum is found in southern China. Illicium mexicanum (Mexican Anise) is native to Mexico. Illicium parviflorum (Yellow Anise) is found in the southeastern United States. Illicium ternstroemioides is native to southern China. Illicium verum (Star Anise) is found in southern China and Vietnam. Uses The fruits of Illicium verum, commonly known as star anise, are widely used as a seasoning in Chinese and Southeast Asian cuisines. In contrast, Japanese star anise (Illicium anisatum) is utilized in Japan for the production of incense. However, the fruits of Japanese star anise are toxic if ingested and should not be consumed.
